title: The Road That Sings Us Home
lyrics:
[Verse 1]
Isaiah told of one safe road
That crosses all the sand;
Be strong, he said, and not afraid,
Your Father holds your hand.

[Chorus]
So walk it strong, so walk it brave,
The desert turns to stream;
And sorrow gathers up its sighs
And flies away from me.

[Verse 2]
Where all the ground was dry and brown
A stream begins to run;
The sad ones leap, the still ones sing,
And sighing comes undone.

[Chorus]

[Verse 3]
The hard thing looked too big today,
My knees were not so strong;
But Father steadied both of them
And helped me walk along.

[Chorus]

[Verse 4]
The road goes on and leads me home,
And singing fills the air;
My feet are slow, my heart is full,
And Father's walking there.

[Chorus]
mood: Promise music. A plain four-square pulse that lands the same way every time, like a sentence a family has said to each other so often nobody has to think about it any more. Hymn-like piano underneath with a faint organ holding the low notes still, and a small lift at the close of each verse that comes back down before the next one starts. It travels from unsteady to planted - the first verse still checking its footing, the last one walking without looking down.
